Evidence: E4, E5, C5, V5.
report.explanation: lc is saturated, and the scheduler gives fa the normalized part p/(p+0.5) and fb 0.5/(p+0.5), using work-conserving unused capacity when fb is not backlogged. fa_goodput_bps rises with p while fb_loss_frac rises once fb's weighted service falls below its 80 Mbps offer. lc.queue.length=1000 does not change steady-state delivered goodputs but lowers measured fb_loss_frac by leaving more packets queued at the measurement boundary. This makes p=0.185 L=1000 feasible, while p=0.186 L=1000 exceeds the loss limit. At this setting fa has enough backlog that fa.type does not change the goal metrics; TcpBbr gives the same measured fa_goodput_bps and fb_loss_frac as TcpCubic.

claims.text: fa_goodput_bps is governed by lc scheduler service and work-conserving unused capacity, not by TCP congestion control when fa has backlog.
The fb_loss_frac <=0.1 constraint binds the optimum: p=0.185 L=1000 is feasible at 0.099905, while p=0.186 L=1000 is infeasible at 0.101361.
lc.queue.length=1000 lowers measured fb_loss_frac without changing delivered goodput by increasing end-of-window queue backlog.
At p=0.185 L=1000, TcpCubic and TcpBbr give identical goal metrics: fa_goodput_bps=26036198 and fb_loss_frac=0.099905.
The best tested feasible fa_goodput_bps is 26036198 at p=0.185 L=1000; p=0.186 L=1000 gives only 26133504, a 0.374% gain inside tolerance, but violates the loss condition.
